story: On a breezy, clear Friday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary and Donna are out on Magnolia Loop, arranging their pickleball doubles at the 1 o'clock courts and agreeing to keep their afternoon plans on schedule. Hal, lost in thought, is tallying the pink flamingos dotting the street while Rosa, content at her dining table, sorts bagged treats and plans the Halloween handout for tomorrow.
events: Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street, for the record
Rosa (rosa dining table): Set out the bagged treats and plan tomorrow's trick-or-treat handout

gary.thought_process: Donna and Hal both invited me and I haven't answered either yet. Donna's courts at 1 works, and Hal's porch lights job can happen after lunch, though I'd have to squeeze it around pickleball. The cart is still waiting on committee sign-off, so no wiring today beyond planning. Hal gets a quick answer now so nobody is left hanging. I'll take the courts at 1 and tell Hal I'll come by after that, since the lights need hauling to the curb before tomorrow's parade anyway.

parameters.content: You're on, Donna. Courts at 1, third-shot drops, and I'll bring my own water. Then I owe Hal some light-hauling, so we'll keep it under the two-hour limit.

donna.thought_process: Gary asked if the courts invitation is still good and I already told him 1 PM, so I shouldn't repeat myself. He's hesitant about touching the cart until the committee signs off, and Hal is right here watching. The sensible move is to confirm 1 PM briefly, reassure him the cart can wait until after practice, and point him to Hal's porch-light job after lunch so his afternoon is sorted. That keeps us on track for the ladder without stepping on code.

parameters.content: Still good, Gary! Courts at 1 sharp, third-shot drops, and we'll be done in plenty of time for Hal's porch lights. Leave the cart alone until the committee says so, and bring water.

hal.thought_process: Gary and Donna are sorting out their pickleball plans, and Gary already said he's keeping his hands off the cart until the committee signs off. I invited him to haul porch lights after lunch last tick, so I shouldn't ask again. I've been counting flamingos and logging cart sketches more than I've been talking to people. Donna got her straight warning already. A flock of flamingos on the street is still L-02 business, but the day before Halloween is a poor time to be a hall monitor. I'll take a look at the flock myself for an accurate count, then decide whether it's really worth the committee's time.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street, for the record

rosa.thought_process: The treats are baked and bagged, my Saturday shift is clear, and nobody is around. Everything for the parade and trick-or-treating is ready on my end. Gary's clamp list and light layout are already in the folder for the review desk, and I'm not going to re-bake or re-ask anyone. The best use of this hour is to stay honest with myself about what's left, so I'll take a quiet moment at the dining table to set out the bags and plan how to hand them out tomorrow between 5 and 7, then check in with Gary and Donna if they turn up.

parameters.content: Set out the bagged treats and plan tomorrow's trick-or-treat handout

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
